arguments.summary: Technical-only, completed-session view (18 Sep 2026; split-adjusted price returns): NVDA has the strongest 63-session leadership versus QQQ and XLK while remaining above its 20/50/200-session averages, but with materially higher realized volatility than QQQ. MU’s strong 5- and 21-session rebound conflicts with 63-session underperformance versus both benchmarks and exceptionally high volatility. QQQ is above all listed averages and has positive short returns, yet remains negative over 63 sessions and trails both SPY and XLK over that window. These are trend/path-risk observations, not forecasts or fundamental recommendations.

claims.text: As of the 18 Sep 2026 completed close, NVDA returned 1.82%/2.16%/5.50% over 5/21/63 sessions and exceeded QQQ by 0.90/1.42/8.08 percentage points and XLK by 0.79/-1.08/6.46 points, respectively. Its close was above its listed 20-, 50-, and 200-session averages.

NVDA’s positive 63-session excess return supports longer-window price leadership versus QQQ, but its 63-session realized volatility of 39.63% versus QQQ’s 20.85% means that leadership came with higher observed path risk; the positive short-window trend does not establish a future outcome.

MU gained 4.16% and 8.40% over 5 and 21 sessions and outperformed QQQ by 3.24 and 7.65 points, but lost 10.42% over 63 sessions and trailed QQQ by 7.83 points (and XLK by 9.46 points). The close was above all listed moving averages.

MU’s short-term rebound is not yet evidence of restored mandate-horizon leadership because its 63-session relative return remains negative and realized volatility was 89.56%, far above QQQ’s 20.85%. This makes the observed path materially less stable than either NVDA or QQQ, without implying an earnings or intrinsic-value conclusion.

QQQ closed above its listed 20-, 50-, and 200-session averages and had positive 5- and 21-session returns, but its 63-session return was -2.59%; it lagged SPY by 4.59 points and XLK by 1.63 points over 63 sessions.

QQQ’s above-average price level and short-window stabilization conflict with its negative 63-session benchmark-relative performance. Accordingly, the supplied data support a stabilization observation, not a conclusion of renewed 63-session leadership.

gaps.description: The fixed panel supplies completed-session returns, moving averages, drawdown and realized volatility, but no volume, intraday behavior, or full return path. Technical conclusions are therefore limited to the supplied daily price-return trend and path-risk measures, not confirmation by participation or support/resistance analysis.

assumptions: All comparisons use the supplied 18 Sep 2026 split-adjusted, SIP-feed completed closes and price-return convention.
The listed moving-average levels are historical snapshots, not future dynamic levels.
Realized volatility describes prior price variation; it is neither a probability nor a fundamental-risk estimate.
arguments.counter_thesis: A close above all listed moving averages can persist despite weak 63-session relative performance; conversely, MU’s sharp short rebound could continue even though it has not repaired its mandate-horizon relative deficit. Neither interpretation establishes causality from prices to company fundamentals.

review_conditions.description: If NVDA records a split-adjusted completed close below 214.2726 (the 18 Sep frozen 50-session average), reassess the positive near-term trend and whether its 63-session excess return versus QQQ remains intact. This is a frozen historical threshold, not a future dynamic average or trade instruction.

If MU records a split-adjusted completed close below 927.2569 (the 18 Sep frozen 50-session average), treat the rebound setup as weakened and recheck whether short-window outperformance is reversing; its high realized volatility makes this test particularly important. This is a frozen historical threshold, not a future dynamic average or trade instruction.

If QQQ records a split-adjusted completed close below 709.9512 (the 18 Sep frozen 50-session average), reassess the short-window stabilization interpretation and its relationship to SPY/XLK. This is a frozen historical threshold, not a future dynamic average or trade instruction.
